resources.string: Starts the artist, album, song or playlist you ask for in Spotify, and your own playlists by name.
Say “play my road trip playlist”, or just “play road trip”. To add one, open it in Spotify, tap Share → Copy link, then Add playlist here. Albums, artists and songs work too.
From Share → Copy link in Spotify

After you ask Cog to play an artist, album, song or playlist on Spotify, this taps the play button on the page Spotify opens, once. It only acts in Spotify, only for a few seconds after you ask, and reads nothing else.

Spotify opens what you ask for but won\'t start it for other apps. This lets Cog tap its play button once, right after you ask; it only works inside Spotify. In the list, pick “Cog: press play in Spotify”. If the switch is greyed out: App info › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings.

Optional. With your own Spotify Client ID, Cog starts the music in Spotify by itself, through Spotify\'s official connection. Registering is free, but Spotify requires the account that registers to have Premium.
1. Open the Spotify developer dashboard, log in, and create an app. Under “Which API/SDKs are you planning to use?”, tick Android.
2. Add the redirect URI below under Redirect URIs, and the package name and SHA1 fingerprint under Android packages.
3. Copy your app\'s Client ID from the dashboard into the field below, tap Connect and allow Cog in Spotify.
A Client ID is 32 letters and numbers
Connected. Music now starts in Spotify by itself.
Spotify hasn\'t allowed it yet. Tap Connect and accept in Spotify.
Couldn\'t connect (%1$s). Check the Client ID, redirect URI, package name and fingerprint in the dashboard.
Tap Connect. Spotify will ask you to allow Cog, once.
Waiting for your OK in Spotify…
Spotify didn\'t answer. Open the Spotify app, make sure you\'re logged in, then tap Connect again.
Spotify said no: %1$s. Check that the dashboard has exactly this redirect URI, package name and fingerprint.
